video_title: Jeff Peterson on working to build an NBA contender and why the Hornets were sold on Kon Knueppel

quotes.speaker: Jeff Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeff Peterson on team building strategies in San Antonio and New York
quotes.excerpt: I don't think there's a right or wrong way. It's just the reality of the situation you're in.

text_blocks.speaker: Adrian Wojnarowski
text_blocks.text: It's always interesting, you see it now between San Antonio and New York. One team is built through the trade and free agency and the other one is built through the draft. I don't think there's a right or wrong way.

text_blocks.speaker: Jeff Peterson
text_blocks.text: I don't think there's a right or wrong way. It's just the reality of the situation you're in.

quotes.speaker: Jeff Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeff Peterson on managing front office time during the busy offseason
quotes.excerpt: This time of year it's so important to be very intentional with your time and be disciplined.
quotes.quote: This time of year it's so important to be very intentional with your time and be disciplined because you have all those variables that you're trying to juggle. You also have some staffing elements, you may have some media obligations, you have your personal family life, things that you got to try to continue to make sure you're not falling behind in those spaces as well.

quotes.speaker: Jeff Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeff Peterson on the nuance and difficulty of making NBA trades
quotes.excerpt: To make a trade is very challenging. The fans think you pick up the phone, but it's nuanced.
quotes.quote: To make a trade is very challenging. I think earlier, sometimes the fans think it's just you pick up the phone, hey, we want to get a deal done, but it's far more nuanced than that as you could imagine. Relationships are the foundation of everything we do, but especially if you want to try to get a deal done.

quotes.speaker: Jeff Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeff Peterson on how new CBA rules impact roster building
quotes.excerpt: The league did a tremendous job in terms of when they wanted to implement these rules.
quotes.quote: The league did a tremendous job in terms of when they wanted to implement these rules to try to create a little bit more parity amongst the league. It's just very restrictive. There's different constraints in terms of how much money you can take back. If you're in the second apron, your pick may be frozen, which in theory just gives teams a little bit more hesitation or extra pause in terms of if we go do this deal, the ramifications are going to be probably much more punitive than they would have been previously. I give credit to Boston and Brad and those guys for the job that they did. They had some constraints last year and they were able to spin out of it and they still had a tremendous season.

quotes.speaker: Jeff Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeff Peterson on the importance of embracing your market's reality
quotes.excerpt: The first thing is embracing the market that you're in and embracing the reality of the situation.
quotes.quote: The first thing is embracing the market that you're in and embracing the reality of the situation. If all is equal, there's a larger group of people or players that would want to be in New York, not just the Knicks, but just want to be in New York versus Charlotte. But then there's also some guys who may like the Charlotte lifestyle and it's a little bit slower. I'm biased now, but it's a tremendous place to be and to raise a family and got everything you need here.

quotes.speaker: Jeff Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeff Peterson on how lottery reform makes drafting more challenging
quotes.excerpt: With these new lottery reform rules, it's going to make it a little bit more challenging.
quotes.quote: With these new lottery reform rules, it's going to make it a little bit more challenging to build through the draft. We're looking at three or four years down the road in terms of just the consequences of what was not the reality in the past. But now that these rules have changed, we got to figure out how to adapt and there's no question that we will.

quotes.speaker: Jeff Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeff Peterson on the difficulty of acquiring stars in smaller markets
quotes.excerpt: In a vacuum, it does make it a bit more challenging for these smaller market teams.
quotes.quote: In a vacuum, it does make it a bit more challenging. It's hard to bottom out because of the new rules. So, I think what you'll see is, if you're in a smaller market, you may have to trade for a star player, and you're making a bet and you're going to give up picks and maybe a player or two, and you just want that star player who wants to be in your market and is going to embrace it.

quotes.speaker: Jeff Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeff Peterson on the evaluation process for Kon Knueppel
quotes.excerpt: He loves basketball. I can't tell you how serious he takes it.
quotes.quote: He loves basketball. I can't tell you how serious he takes it. He's a historian of the game. He just loves basketball. We were fortunate that the ACC tournament was here that season and Cooper Flagg unfortunately had an injury and Kon, they put the ball in his hands even more and he was able to shoulder the load and again, that was just another layer to the whole thing that the guy is fiercely competitive and he wanted that challenge, which was very encouraging to see.

quotes.speaker: Jeff Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeff Peterson on what 'processing the game well' means for players
quotes.excerpt: The game is more read and react. You need guys that can think the game in real time.
quotes.quote: In today's age, the game is more read and react. It's no longer I'm going to come down the court and run punch five and I'm going to throw it into the post and this guy is going to back down. You need guys that can think the game in real time and read and react and process the game. I think the better off you are. We're constantly trying to evaluate, is the player simply making the right read for the team, not just for himself, but for his team.

quotes.speaker: Jeff Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeff Peterson on the collaborative relationship with Charles Lee
quotes.excerpt: Charles and his entire coaching staff, they can come into any front office meeting that we have.
quotes.quote: Charles and his entire coaching staff, they can come into any front office meeting that we have. We're not hiding anything. There aren't any silos in this organization and conversely, I know that if I wanted to go to any of the coaches' meetings, I could pop in there as well, which I don't because I would mess the whole thing up. But it's the ability for us to disagree, because we certainly have our disagreements, but at the end of the day, we know that after that disagreement, we can go get a glass of wine.
